1.title: Security Alerting and Monitoring
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Security Alerting and Monitoring. It covers the exam area Security Operations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. What is monitored. Monitoring activities. Tools. Protocols and data sources. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Security Operations (twenty-seven percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Security plus S Y zero eight oh one V eight exam objectives.

1.title: What is monitored
1.text: What is monitored. Systems. Servers, endpoints, C P U, memory, disk, sign-ins. Applications. Errors, transactions, access, performance. Infrastructure. Network devices, firewalls, traffic, cloud services.

1.title: Monitoring activities
1.text: Monitoring activities. Log aggregation. Collect logs from many sources into one place. Alerting. Notify staff when a rule or threshold is met. Scanning. Regular checks for vulnerabilities and drift. Archiving. Keep logs for the required time (legal and investigation needs). Reporting. Summaries for managers and auditors. Alert tuning. Adjust rules to cut false positives without missing real threats.

1.title: Monitoring activities, continued
1.text: Monitoring activities. The figure shows this: Logs flow from systems into aggregation, correlation and alerts, then to analysts. Exam tip: Too many false alarms cause alert fatigue, so teams tune alerts: raise thresholds, add context, remove duplicates. Aggregation allows correlation across sources.

1.title: Tools
1.text: Tools. Benchmarks. Standard secure configurations (for example C I S) to measure against. Agents or agentless. Agent-based collection uses software on the device (more detail); agentless collects remotely (nothing to install). sim. Security information and event management: collects, correlates and alerts on logs from many sources. Antivirus. Detects and removes known malware. D L P. Detects and blocks sensitive data leaving. Vulnerability scanners. Find weaknesses. Orchestration. Automates workflows across tools (soar, module sixteen). Packet analyzer. Captures and inspects network packets (for example Wireshark).

1.title: Protocols and data sources
1.text: Protocols and data sources. net flow. Summaries of network conversations (who talked to whom, how much). S N M P. Simple Network Management Protocol: monitors and manages network devices (use S N M Pv three for security). sys log. Standard way to send logs to a central server. scap. Security Content Automation Protocol: standard formats to automate checking configuration and vulnerabilities. Port mirroring. A switch copies traffic to a monitoring port (for I D S or analyzers). Automated alerts. Rule-based alerts by email, text or ticket. Dashboards. Visual summary of status. Network management systems. Central tools to monitor device health. Exam tip: sim equals collect, correlate, alert. net flow equals traffic metadata, not content. Port mirroring (S P A N) feeds a sensor with a copy of traffic. sys log equals log transport. scap equals automation of compliance checks.

1.title: Protocols and data sources, continued
1.text: Protocols and data sources. Exam tip: A sim is only as good as the logs it receives and the rules that are tuned: collect from all key sources and tune alerts.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants logs from firewalls, servers and applications gathered in one place so that events can be correlated. What should it deploy? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A sim. A sim aggregates logs, correlates events and raises alerts.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Analysts ignore alerts because most are harmless. What activity should be performed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Alert tuning. Tuning reduces false positives so real alerts are noticed.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A security team needs a copy of all traffic on a switch for an intrusion detection sensor. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Port mirroring. Port mirroring sends a copy of traffic to the monitoring port.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which data source shows which hosts talked to each other and how much data moved, without storing packet content? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: net flow. net flow records conversation summaries and metadata.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A company wants monitoring on laptops that gives detailed local data and works even when they are off the V P N (virtual private network). Which collection method fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Agent-based collection. An installed agent can collect detailed local data wherever the device is.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which protocol sends log messages from devices to a central log server? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: sys log. Syslog is the standard way to forward logs to a central server.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does a sim do? Answer: Collects, correlates and alerts on logs from many sources. Question two. What is alert tuning? Answer: Adjusting alert rules to reduce false positives while catching real threats. Question three. What does net flow provide? Answer: Summaries of network conversations.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the difference between agent-based and agentless? Answer: Agent-based uses software on the device; agentless collects remotely. Question five. What is scap for? Answer: Automating checks of configuration and vulnerabilities with standard formats. Question six. What is log archiving for? Answer: Keeping logs for the required time for investigations and compliance.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Scope: systems, applications, infrastructure. Activities: aggregation, alerting, scanning, archiving, reporting, alert tuning. Tools: benchmarks, agents or agentless, sim, antivirus, D L P, scanners, orchestration, packet analyzer. Protocols and sources: net flow (metadata), S N M P, sys log, scap, port mirroring, dashboards, network management systems. In the next module, we continue the course.
